text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key rule is to follow naming conventions: use clear, meaningful names for variables and functions, so others can quickly see what they do. It is also good practice to keep functions small and focused on one task. When code is simple and well-organized, it becomes much easier to maintain. You can fix bugs, add new features, and update the program without confusion. In short, clean code saves time and helps teams work together more effectively.
